prompt_text: Where should I buy tires in Pleasanton CA and who does the best installation?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — quick question first: what vehicle (make/model/year) and what kind of driving do you do (commute, highway, performance, light truck/off‑road)? That lets me recommend tires and more targeted installers.

Short answer — where to buy and who usually does the best installation in the Pleasanton / Tri‑Valley area

- Discount Tire (serves Livermore/Pleasanton area): wide selection, competitive pricing, good installation turnaround, flat repair/road hazard options depending on tire.
- Costco Tire Center (nearest Costco locations in the Tri‑Valley): often best price on name-brand tires and includes mounting/balancing + road hazard warranty — requires a Costco membership and appointments can fill up.
- Firestone Complete Auto Care (Pleasanton area): solid chain shop that does mounting, balancing, alignment and inspections; convenient for alignment/service combos.
- Les Schwab / independent local tire shops: many independent shops in Pleasanton/Dublin/Livermore get excellent local reviews and can offer very hands‑on service and advice — often better for specialty tires, light trucks, or custom installs.

Which installer is “best”
- For consistent, reliable installs: Discount Tire and Costco are usually top picks (if you have a Costco membership). They have standardized training and wide experience.
- For specialty needs (performance tires, light truck, custom wheels) or more personalized service: highly rated local independent shops often do the best job.
- For overall value: compare the all‑in price (tires + mounting + balancing + valve stems + taxes + disposal + alignment) and any included warranties.

What to check / ask any shop before you buy
- Is the price quoted “all‑in” (mounting, balancing, new valve stems, tire disposal, taxes)?
- Do they include a road‑hazard warranty, free rotation, or free flat repairs? If so, for how long?
- Do they perform road‑force or just static balancing? (Road‑force is better for runout issues.)
- Are wheel alignment checks/alignments available same‑day and how much extra?
- Do they service the TPMS (sensor reprogramming/replacement) if needed?
- Are techs ASE certified? How long has the shop been open? Any guarantee on installation (lug torque, re‑check after 50–100 miles)?
- Appointment wait time — some places do walk‑ins, chains fill quickly, Costco often requires appointments.

Tips for the day of installation
- Bring your vehicle’s manual for recommended torque specs if you want to confirm lug torque.
- Ask them to torque lug nuts to spec and to re‑check lug torque after ~50–100 miles.
- Inspect tires/wheels before leaving (no obvious defects, proper valve stems, wheel weights in place).
- Keep all paperwork and warranty info.

If you want I can:
- Recommend specific tire models for your vehicle and driving style.
- Look up current top‑rated tire shops in Pleasanton and return a short list (I’ll need permission to perform a live search or you can tell me if you want me to use Google/Yelp results). 

Which would you like me to do next?
